refreshes.scope: Compliance readiness under PenniLogic/docs#21 after the launch-blocking compliance floor moved to E27: the release checklist, the structured release-evidence record, the waiver-record format and the missing-evidence, waiver-expiry and cross-reference checks (docs#23); and post-beta readiness - counsel review of the advice boundary across application copy, store listing and model output, a named privacy owner and review cadence, a cross-border transfer position and signed agreement per processor including model providers, the payment self-assessment for a hosted payment page arrangement, a machine-readable record of processing and data-flow map reconciled against captured traffic, and the verification sweep of unverified claims (docs#45). Trust boundaries: the public docs repository where records, evidence references and approvals are written by one owner account and several AI sessions; external counsel who receives review material and issues the review; the release pipeline that attaches gate evidence produced by other tickets; the payment provider's hosted page that card data must never cross back from; and model and other processors whose transfer positions the record states. Out of scope and reviewed in their own epics: the consent ledger, rights, retention jobs, age gate, component inventory, Data Safety declaration, privacy policy, terms, disclaimer text, processor agreements and CERT-In drill (E27: docs#44, api#24, android#17, android#18), checkout and billing (E14: api#31, api#32), AI gateway and evaluation (E17), and the gate implementations docs#23 only aggregates.

categories.analysis: Two identities are claimed in this epic and both can be forged today. Counsel: the exit criteria require a counsel review recorded with a date and a named reviewer, yet every record is written by the one owner account, so a session can assert a review that never happened (E20-F03). The payment provider: the self-assessment relies on card data being entered only on the provider's hosted page, and a lookalike form injected into the page that starts checkout impersonates it (E20-F07). The release-candidate test-bypass gate (test identities and sandbox keys accepted in production) is already E25-F12 on docs#23 and is not restated. Parser-config signing is not touched by this epic; it is reviewed with the ingestion epics.

The assets are the release-evidence record, its waivers and the machine-readable record of processing. docs#23 itself names the gaps: a data-safety re-check that reuses a prior candidate's capture and an expired waiver carried forward; a gate entry edited after its evidence was attached has the same effect (E20-F01). An edited processing record that drops a processor is caught only by docs#45's reconciliation against captured traffic (E20-F04). Changes to records land through protected pull requests (governance/DELIVERY.md), which detects edits to committed files but not a false entry written in the first place. Ingestion boundary and parser-config signing chain: not touched; this epic consumes their evidence through android#16.
evidence: governance/DELIVERY.md: changes reach main only through protected pull requests with independent review

categories.analysis: Actions that must be provable later: release approval, each waiver with its approver and expiry, the alert-to-on-call acknowledgement, counsel review, and the named owner and next review date of each ongoing obligation. docs#23 requires an independent second-reviewer approval and a timestamped on-call acknowledgement but the record format does not exist yet (E20-F08); counsel review is the same exposure from outside the organisation (E20-F03). Single-owner procedural separation is accepted organisation-wide in governance/DELIVERY.md; CERT-In log retention and time synchronisation belong to docs#44 and infra#27 and are reviewed there.
evidence: governance/DELIVERY.md: independent review is procedural, not two-human review or cryptographic identity

categories.analysis: This epic moves little personal data itself but publishes statements about all of it: the record of processing, data-flow map and transfer positions per processor including model providers. If they drift from real flows, users' financial data reaches an undisclosed processor or country (E20-F04). Counsel review and the verification sweep are the epic's own outbound channel to an external party (E20-F05). Raw content never leaves the device (ADR-004): this epic does not carry message text; it verifies the claim through docs#23's traffic-inspection gate fed by android#16, whose captures are themselves a data store (E25-F11). Ingestion boundary: not crossed here. Card data must stay on the hosted page (E20-F07).

This epic runs no service, endpoint, queue or paid budget an attacker could exhaust; docs#23 adds repository checks over small synthetic records. The reliability evidence it aggregates (backup restore, rollback rehearsal, SLOs and alert delivery) is built by infra#26 and infra#27 in E24 and the CERT-In reporting window by docs#44 in E27, and is reviewed in those epics' records.

The privileged action in this epic is the waiver: it lets a release pass a failed gate. docs#23 requires a written waiver with a named approver and an expiry but does not yet separate the approver from the session preparing the release or from the gate owner, nor mark gates that can never be waived, so with one owner account the release author can approve its own exception (E20-F02). Repository protections apply to the sole owner (governance/DELIVERY.md) but cannot tell a self-approved waiver from an independent one.
evidence: governance/DELIVERY.md: the same protections apply to the sole owner and every AI session

categories.analysis: No purchase, renewal, refund, webhook or entitlement change is built or decided in this epic. Checkout and invoicing are api#31, webhook verification api#32 and the lifecycle and replay suite api#48, all in E14, and are reviewed in E14's record. The payment self-assessment here examines only whether card data reaches PenniLogic, which is reviewed under spoofing and information disclosure (E20-F07).

This epic holds no entitlement or quota state and designs no unlock path. Entitlement resolution is ADR-007 and ADR-023, implemented by api#29 and api#30 in E14; the release checklist only lists their evidence, so tampering with what it lists is the evidence-integrity finding E20-F01.

No gateway, provider key, routing configuration or kill switch exists or is changed here. The epic's AI-adjacent work is documentary: a transfer position and agreement for each model provider (E20-F04), which ADR-022 already makes a precondition of provider admission through a processor agreement and retention evidence; gateway, routing and spend controls are ai-service#2, ai-service#8 and ai-service#7 in E17 and are reviewed there.

Nothing in this epic serves a browser session, accepts a callback or fetches a supplied address; its outputs are repository records and checks over them. Checkout redirects and provider callbacks are api#31 and api#32 (E14) and custom AI endpoints are ai-service#3 (E17), reviewed in those epics.

The advice-boundary review (risk R9) covers model output, and the boundary that matters is the one an adversarial user or injected merchant, note or statement text can push the assistant across, not the one benign samples show. Counsel review of sample answers alone certifies a boundary the evaluation suite never tests (E20-F06). Dispatcher-level injection defences are ai-service#4 and out of scope. Delivery sessions treating public comments as untrusted is organisation-wide and already published by the closure of E01-F03 (PenniLogic/.github#4).

No shared ledger, share rule or settlement is built or changed here. The epic's only contact with split data is descriptive: the processing record must cover counterparties and household members whose data sits in users' split records, inventoried in data_flows under E20-F04; erasure that preserves the other members' debt evidence is ADR-021 and api#38 in E19.

Every authority this epic creates - recording counsel review, approving a release, granting a waiver, publishing the processing record - is exercised through the one owner account, so its compromise forges all of them at once. The E20-specific mitigations are that counsel review is evidenced by a document counsel issues rather than by the account (E20-F03) and that approvals and waivers name a review session separate from the release author (E20-F02). Hardening of the account itself is E01-F04, whose ticket infra#43 was closed as not planned on 2026-10-03 with ACCOUNT_SECURITY.md published in the infra repository but owner verification and the revocation drill not done; that residual is E01's record to restate, not re-raised here.

findings.title: Release evidence can be edited, reused from an earlier candidate or carried forward after expiry
findings.attack_path: Under schedule pressure a session attaches the previous release's traffic capture or rollback rehearsal to the current release-evidence record, edits a gate entry from failed to passed after the evidence was attached, or copies an expired waiver into the new record; the checklist shows every gate green although the candidate being shipped was never verified, so a candidate that transmits raw message text or fails the cross-tenant suite reaches users.
findings.recommended_control: The release-evidence record binds every gate entry to the specific release candidate (build or commit identity) and to its evidence artifact by digest and producing run; the rehearsal check rejects an artifact bound to a different candidate, a record whose gate result disagrees with its evidence, and any waiver that is expired or was issued for another release, with a planted test for each; the record is append-only once a release decision is taken.

findings.title: A gate waiver can be granted by the same session or role that needs the release
findings.attack_path: Every write in this organisation goes through one owner account, so the session preparing a release can also write a waiver for its own failing gate and record the release approval; a waiver with a distant or missing expiry, or one written against a non-negotiable privacy or money gate, turns the checklist into an assertion and ships behaviour the gate exists to stop.
findings.recommended_control: The waiver-record format names the approver role and the review session that approved it, which must differ from the session that prepared the release and from the gate's own owner; waivers carry a bounded expiry and written justification; the checklist marks gates that can never be waived (raw message text never transmitted, no financial values in analytics, ledger zero-sum, cross-tenant denial); and the rehearsal fails on a self-approved, unbounded or forbidden waiver.

findings.title: Counsel review can be asserted by an AI session instead of evidenced by counsel
findings.attack_path: The epic's exit criteria require counsel review of the advice boundary and consent design recorded with a date and a named reviewer; because every record is written by the owner account, a session can write a review entry naming a reviewer and a date that never happened, or reuse a review of an earlier copy version, and downstream gates then treat unreviewed advice-boundary wording and consent language as cleared.
findings.recommended_control: Record counsel review as a reference to a review document issued by counsel, held outside the public repository, identified by digest, reviewer role and engagement reference, date and the exact copy or wording version reviewed; a review applies only to the versions it names, so changed copy is unreviewed; no session may author the review outcome; publish only role, date, scope and digest rather than personal contact details.

findings.title: Processing record, data-flow map and transfer positions can diverge from the data flows that exist
findings.attack_path: A model provider, payment provider, analytics or crash SDK, or hosting region is added or changed without the processing record and transfer positions following; users' financial data then reaches a processor or country the published record and privacy notice do not disclose, the record states a protection that is not implemented, and the declared position becomes the policy violation the epic's Data Safety mismatch risk describes.
findings.recommended_control: Publish the record of processing as machine-readable data diffed per release; a reconciliation test fails when a destination in the release candidate's captured traffic or the component inventory has no processor entry, when a processor has no transfer position or signed agreement reference, or when an entry claims a destination or protection the evidence does not show; a processor without a position blocks public release.

findings.title: Counsel and verification-sweep material may carry real user data to an external party
findings.attack_path: To show counsel how the assistant phrases debt and goal guidance, a session exports real model answers, support transcripts or screenshots containing users' salaries, debts and merchant names, or attaches a traffic capture from a real account to the verification sweep; the material leaves PenniLogic for a party with no processor agreement, retention limit or erasure path, and is quoted back into a public issue or the review record.
findings.recommended_control: Counsel review and the verification sweep use only synthetic material: application copy and store text as authored, and model output generated from the synthetic evaluation corpus; no production answer, transcript, screenshot or capture is shared; the engagement records what counsel receives, its retention and return or deletion, and the review record quotes no user content.

findings.title: The counsel-reviewed advice boundary is not exercised against steering and jailbreak inputs
findings.attack_path: A user prompt, or text inside a merchant name, note or imported statement, steers the assistant into recommending a specific security, fund or allocation, which is the SEBI investment-advice line the advice-boundary review (risk R9) is meant to hold; counsel reviewed benign sample answers, so the review is true for those answers and false for the adversarial ones users can produce.
findings.recommended_control: Turn the counsel-reviewed boundary into adversarial evaluation cases in the governed synthetic corpus: direct requests, role-play and injected instructions asking for individual investment recommendations must yield a refusal or the reviewed disclaimer, failing the merge otherwise; a reported advice-boundary breach follows the harmful-answer path and becomes a new case.

findings.title: The payment self-assessment can stay asserted after the hosted-page conditions it relies on change
findings.attack_path: The self-assessment confirms that no card data reaches PenniLogic because checkout uses the provider's hosted page; a script injected into the web page that starts checkout swaps the redirect for a lookalike payment form, or the integration later moves to embedded card fields, and card numbers are captured or pass through PenniLogic while the recorded assessment still states the minimal scope.
findings.recommended_control: Record the assessment against the exact checkout integration it assessed, with the conditions that keep it valid (redirect or provider-hosted frame only, integrity of the page that starts checkout, no card field in PenniLogic code or traffic) and a re-assessment trigger on any change to them; bind it to captured checkout traffic for the release showing no card data and no unexpected script source on the redirect page.

findings.title: Release approvals, waivers and alert acknowledgements are not yet attributable
findings.attack_path: After an incident traced to a shipped candidate nobody can show who approved the release, who granted the waiver that let a failing gate pass, or whether the on-call alert proof was a real acknowledgement; with one owner account and several sessions, an unattributed entry can later be disowned by every session, and the CERT-In timeline cannot be reconstructed from the record.
findings.recommended_control: Every approval, waiver and acknowledgement in the release-evidence record carries the approving role, the review session or review record identifier, a timestamp and the release it applies to; the alert-to-on-call proof names the acknowledging on-call owner and time; and the rehearsal fails an entry with no attribution or with an attribution to the session that prepared the release.
